smell verb

give off a smell

also smell of, smell good, smell nice, smell bad, it smells

classical

Cic. Att. 2.1.1: bene olēre
Ter. Ad. 1.2.37: olet unguenta (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 381

oleō, olēre, oluī

verb, second conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

smell, smell of

What something smells of is in the accusative: olet unguenta, “he smells of scent” (Ter.), crocum olēre (Cic. de Or. 3.99). Bene olēre, male olēre: to smell good, to smell bad.

Other words

  • redoleō, redolēre, redoluī — give off a scent, smell strongly of

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. G. 4.169: redolentque thymō frāgrantia mella · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • et, ut mulierēs, ideō bene olēre quia nihil olēbant vidēbantur.

    and, like women, they seemed to smell good precisely because they smelled of nothing.Cic. Att. 2.1.1

  • Postume, nōn bene olet quī bene semper olet.

    Postumus, a man who always smells good doesn’t smell good.Mart. 2.12.4

  • fīla Tarentīnī graviter redolentia porrī ēdistī quotiēns, ōscula clūsa datō.

    whenever you’ve eaten threads of strong-smelling Tarentine leek, kiss with your mouth shut.Mart. 13.18.1–2

  • bene (male) olēre

    to smell good (bad)Traupman 381

See also smell, smell, sense, nose, yucky.
